item.text: {"decisions":[{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0001","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Pure identity metadata (name, dates, party affiliation, update note). No economic governance content. Excluded.","exclusion_reason":"Chunk contains only biographical identity metadata with no policy content whatsoever. No mention of economic agenda, budgets, fiscal rules, employment, taxation, or any subject bearing on questions 5B.1-5B.10."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0002","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.10"],"relevance_strength":"weak","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0003","unit-0004"],"explanation":"Reports 2018 electoral victory with 53.2% of votes. Confirms AMLO secured the presidency and absolute coalition majority in both congressional chambers, establishing the policy-making mandate for 2018-2024. The mandate period and parliamentary majority are foundational conditions for economic governance (5B.1 legislative capacity; 5B.10 whether trajectory was strengthened). Information is summary rather than policy-specific.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0003","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.7"],"relevance_strength":"weak","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0002","unit-0004"],"explanation":"Covers 2006 presidential race where AMLO lost by 0.56% and subsequently claimed electoral fraud, declared himself 'legitimate president,' and led civil disobedience. The claim of 'robo' (theft/fraud) in the electoral process is documented evidence of his public framing of governance failure (5B.7 reliability of institutions; 5B.1 quality of democratic process as part of broad-based governance). Not economic policy per se, but his framing of institutional failure bears on his diagnostic approach to governance.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0004","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.4"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0003","unit-0005"],"explanation":"Documents AMLO's political trajectory from PRD split in September 2012, founding of MORENA, and his systematic opposition to Peña Nieto's structural reforms — specifically the energy reform (energética), educational reform (educativa), labor reform (laboral), and telecommunications reform (telecomunicaciones). His stated opposition to 'neoliberalismo creador de inequidades' and defense of state-owned Pemex maps to 5B.3 (credible fiscal/energy rules) and 5B.4 (fair competition/property rules). The rejection of the Pact by Mexico (PRI-PAN-PRD) documents his policy divergence from mainstream economic consensus.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0005","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.2","5B.3","5B.4","5B.5","5B.6","5B.8","5B.9","5B.10"],"relevance_strength":"pivotal","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0004","unit-0006"],"explanation":"Presents the full 2018 electoral program (Proyecto 2018) as the candidate of Juntos Haremos Historia coalition. Contains multiple specific policy pledges directly mapped to 5B questions: 'austeridad republicana' to redirect public resources without tax increases (5B.1, 5B.3); combatting poverty and elevating human development of vulnerable groups (5B.1, 5B.8, 5B.10); increasing domestic gasoline production to reduce imports and prices (5B.3, 5B.4); energy and food self-sufficiency with guaranteed prices for local producers (5B.4, 5B.8); eradication of political corruption 'giving example' from Los Pinos (5B.5); gradual withdrawal of armed forces with goal to 'pacify' Mexico in three years — shock response framework (5B.9). This is the most concrete economic governance platform document in the source.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0006","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.4"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0005","unit-0007"],"explanation":"Documents how AMLO presented himself as a pragmatic social democracy 'assumptions orthodox notions of free market, macroeconomic stability, budgetary discipline, and peso flotation' while rejecting privatization and prioritizing national production. This defines his economic model bearing on 5B.1 (legislative agenda), 5B.3 (monetary/fiscal rules), and 5B.4 (investment/competition framework). Also documents his pledge to address corruption of former presidents 'without vengeance or hatred' and his conservative positions on abortion and same-sex marriage. Documents his December 1, 2018 inauguration and early policy gestures (Guardia Nacional creation, pre-inaugural consultations).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0007","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.3","5B.9"],"relevance_strength":"weak","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0006","unit-0008"],"explanation":"Covers October 2018 context including USMCA trade deal negotiations (AMLO considered beneficial), migration caravans, and Trump border threats. The USMCA is a concrete trade/regulatory agreement with direct bearing on Mexico's economic rules (5B.3) and shock management in US-Mexico relations (5B.9). AMLO's offer of work visas to migrants is documented as a policy response to a socioeconomic shock (5B.9).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0008","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Table of contents for the biography. No substantive content. Excluded.","exclusion_reason":"Chunk is a table of contents listing 10 section headings with no substantive policy content. No economic governance information."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0009","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Birth, family background, 1953 birth in Tabasco, move to Villahermosa, family store. 1969 brother death incident. Pure biographical content with no economic governance evidence.","exclusion_reason":"Chunk covers childhood, family background, death of brother in 1969. No content related to economic policy, budgets, fiscal rules, or any question in 5B.1-5B.10."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0010","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"AMLO's move to Mexico City in 1972, enrollment at UNAM Faculty of Political Sciences, PRI political socialization, 1976 campaign work for Carlos Pellicer. Pure political biography with no economic governance content.","exclusion_reason":"Chunk covers UNAM enrollment and PRI political work beginning in 1976. No content related to economic governance questions 5B.1-5B.10."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0011","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"AMLO's career advancement within PRI through direct party placement system. Delegation at INI in La Chontalpa working with indigenous communities, director of Sectoral Studies at state promotion secretariat. Social work but not economic governance policy. Also covers his university teaching and marriage to Rocío Beltrán.","exclusion_reason":"Chunk covers early PRI career functionary positions (INI delegation, Secretary of Promotion) and family life. No economic governance policy content relevant to questions 5B.1-5B.10."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0012","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"1978-1982 period: COPLAMAR delegation, indigenous language publications, agricultural programs, university teaching, birth of children. Also covers 1982 CEPES work for Gonzalez Pedrero campaign. Social and administrative background, not economic governance policy.","exclusion_reason":"Chunk covers COPLAMAR work, university teaching, and campaign work for Enrique Gonzalez Pedrero. No substantive economic governance content for 5B questions."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0013","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"AMLO's role as Tabasco PRI president in 1983, his ideological dogmatism on the left, removal from position in November 1983, subsequent Mexico City consumer protection function (INCO), publication of historical book on Tabasco, UNAM graduation in 1987 with thesis on Mexican state formation, joining Corriente Democratica within PRI. Political biography with no specific economic governance content.","exclusion_reason":"Chunk covers party political career within PRI, removal from Tabasco party position, INCO function, book publication, and UNAM graduation. No specific economic governance policy content for 5B questions."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0014","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Covers Corriente Democratica formation in 1987 with Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas and Porfirio Muñoz Ledo, 1988 electoral alliance with FDN coalition, Cárdenas presidential run and AMLO gubernatorial run in Tabasco, alleged electoral fraud. Political history, not economic governance.","exclusion_reason":"Chunk covers founding of Corriente Democratica and 1988 electoral alliance. No specific content on economic governance for 5B questions."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0015","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"PRD founding in May 1989, AMLO as Tabasco PRD president, 1991 democratic exodus march from Villahermosa to Mexico City. Political biography of opposition movement, not economic governance.","exclusion_reason":"Chunk covers PRD founding and 1991 march for democracy. No specific economic governance content for questions 5B.1-5B.10."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0016","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"1994 Tabasco gubernatorial election loss to Roberto Madrazo (38.7% vs 57.5%), electoral protest, 1995 democratic caravan, creation of Alianza Nacional Democratica. Political opposition history, not economic governance policy.","exclusion_reason":"Chunk covers 1994 electoral loss and subsequent protest activity. No specific content on economic governance for 5B questions."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0017","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"AMLO elected PRD president in July 1996 with 73.9% of votes, publication of book on Tabasco corruption, FOBAPROA critique. Contains FOBAPROA reference which is an economic/financial instrument, but treatment is political biography framing rather than analysis of his economic governance approach.","exclusion_reason":"Chunk covers PRD party presidency election and book publication. While FOBAPROA is mentioned, the context is biographical rather than policy analysis of AMLLO's economic governance approach."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0018","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"PRD electoral successes 1997-1999 (Cárdenas DF victory, assembly and federal congressional wins), April 1999 AMLO steps down as PRD president, FOBAPROA book published. Political party history, not economic governance.","exclusion_reason":"Chunk covers PRD electoral victories 1997-1999 and party leadership transition. No specific economic governance content for 5B questions."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0019","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","5B.7","5B.8"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0018","unit-0020"],"explanation":"Covers AMLO's 2000-2005 term as Head of Government of Mexico City (DF). Contains evidence of: (1) vigorous public works campaign for urban infrastructure (5B.6); (2) social protection programs including Pensión Universal Alimenticia para Adultos Mayores — a direct social transfer program with incidence across classes (5B.1, 5B.6, 5B.8); (3) commitment to regular accountability, transparency, and participatory democracy (5B.7). Also documents opposition criticism of populist budget management. This is the only unit covering actual executive governance by AMLO before the 2018 presidency.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0020","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Political image analysis: pejelagarto nickname, AMLO moniker, characterization of his oratorical style and use of 'mañaneras' press conferences. Political characterization rather than policy content.","exclusion_reason":"Chunk covers political image, nicknames, and media strategy. No substantive economic governance policy content for 5B questions."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0021","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","5B.7","5B.8"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0020","unit-0022"],"explanation":"Continuation of DF government coverage: vigorous public works campaign for urban infrastructure improvement and expansion, social protection programs including standout Pensión Universal Alimenticia para Adultos Mayores, refusal to implement Seguro Popular citing already-provided free municipal social coverage. These document actual policy delivery in governance (5B.1 broad-based prosperity, 5B.6 infrastructure and service delivery, 5B.7 transparency, 5B.8 incidence across groups).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0022","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Videoescándalo breakdown: March 2004 Televisa broadcast of clandestine videos showing PRD politicians including René Bejarano, Carlos Ímaz, and Rosario Robles engaged in corruption (money laundering, extortion with Carlos Ahumada Kurtz). Party political scandal rather than evidence of economic governance policy.","exclusion_reason":"Chunk covers the 2004 video scandal involving corruption by PRD subordinates (Bejarano, Ímaz, Robles). This is a scandal affecting AMLO's party, not evidence of his economic governance policies. The political conspiracy framing is his response, not a policy document."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0023","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.5","5B.7"],"relevance_strength":"weak","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0022","unit-0024"],"explanation":"Documents AMLO's response to the videoescándalo: he condemned the corrupt practices but his reaction was late and lukewarm, reserving emphasis for a political counterattack claiming 'conspiracy' by ex-president Salinas, Fernández de Cevallos, and the Fox administration. Documents his reframing of corruption scandals as political persecution (bearing on 5B.5 how he handles corruption allegations against connected actors; 5B.7 how he responds to evidence of failure).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0024","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"PGR desafuero request in May 2004 based on minor land expropriation case from 2000 Cuajimalpa. Legal/constitutional dispute rather than economic governance. PRD accusation that the challenge was politically motivated to block 2006 presidential candidacy.","exclusion_reason":"Chunk covers the desafuero legal process related to a land expropriation case. This is a legal/constitutional dispute with no substantive economic governance policy content for 5B questions."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0025","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"August 2004 demonstration of 200,000 PRD supporters in Zócalo, October 2004 book publication 'Un proyecto alternativo de nación,' November 2004 Fox dismissal of Marcelo Ebrard as Security Secretary. Political mobilization and book announcement rather than governance policy.","exclusion_reason":"Chunk covers political mobilization against desafuero, book publication announcement, and Ebrard dismissal. No substantive economic governance policy content for 5B questions."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0026","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"April 2005 Chamber of Deputies vote approving desafuero (360-127), PRD mobilization, legal defense, and April 25 return to office after PGR failed to secure judicial processing. Political/legal drama of the desafuero, not economic governance.","exclusion_reason":"Chunk covers the congressional desafuero vote and subsequent mobilization. Political/legal process with no substantive economic governance policy content for 5B questions."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0027","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"April-May 2005: PGR inability to initiate criminal proceedings emboldens AMLO; Fox accepts attorney general resignation; May 4 new prosecutor drops charges and files case; Fox-Lopez Obrador meeting; July 2005 AMLO requests leave from DF government to focus on PRD primary. Political resolution of desafuero crisis.","exclusion_reason":"Chunk covers resolution of the desafuero crisis. No substantive economic governance policy content for 5B questions."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0028","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"PRD primary: AMLO's uncontested nomination as presidential candidate of Coalición Por el Bien de Todos (PRD, PT, Convergencia) in September 2005, withdrawal of Cárdenas. December 2005 registration with IFE. Campaign kickoff in Metlatónoc Guerrero January 2006. Political nomination history.","exclusion_reason":"Chunk covers nomination process and campaign launch. No substantive economic governance policy content for 5B questions."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0029","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.5"],"relevance_strength":"weak","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0028","unit-0030"],"explanation":"Campaign content: AMLO accused Calderón of nepotism, abuse of functions, and influence trafficking as BANOBRAS director and Energy Secretary under Fox. Accusations of 'FeCal' (nepotistic/elite candidate) and claims that Calderón represented continuity of neoliberal policies. These are specific corruption/nepotism allegations bearing on 5B.5 (accountability for connected actors) and 5B.1 (whether elite capture characterizes his opponent's governance).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0030","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.5","5B.10"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0029","unit-0031"],"explanation":"Coalición Por el Bien de Todos platform: 'robo,' 'corrupción,' and 'privilegios' as systemic diagnoses of the federal government; FOBAPROA characterized as 'privatization of gains and socialization of losses'; anti-corruption commitment ('limpiar al gobierno de arriba hacia abajo'); reduction of presidential salary by half; investigation of former presidents' corruption. Direct evidence of AMLLO's economic governance diagnosis and policy platform bearing on 5B.1 (corruption as systemic rent-seeking), 5B.5 (anti-corruption enforcement intentions), and 5B.10 (assessment of inherited trajectory).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0031","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Campaign platform continuation: social programs, PRD defense of constitutional right to 'justo' wage, position on NAFTA renegotiation and migration. Some economic policy content but framed as electoral program rather than implemented policy, and covered in more detail in subsequent units. Weak relevance to 5B questions compared to other more substantive units.","exclusion_reason":"Chunk covers campaign platform continuation including social programs, wage rights, and NAFTA position. Content is electoral campaign material with limited specificity on actual implementation. More detailed economic policy content is covered in subsequent units (unit-0046, unit-0047, unit-0062)."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0032","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Pre-election polling data and AMLO's stated position on Hugo Chávez / Venezuela. Electoral positioning, not economic governance.","exclusion_reason":"Chunk covers pre-election polling data and Venezuela positioning. No substantive economic governance policy content for 5B questions."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0033","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.7","5B.10"],"relevance_strength":"weak","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0032","unit-0034"],"explanation":"Official IFE results: Calderón 35.89%, AMLO 35.31%, margin 243,934 votes (0.58%). AMLO's demand for full ballot recount claiming 50,000 ballot boxes showed irregularities. Documents his institutional challenge process bearing on 5B.7 (confidence in electoral/institutional information) and his framing of the inherited democratic system (5B.10).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0034","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.7","5B.10"],"relevance_strength":"weak","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0033","unit-0035"],"explanation":"International election observation missions (EU, OAS, UN) confirming electoral cleanliness. AMLO rejected these assessments and continued to claim fraud. Documents his relationship with independent evaluation/international auditing (bearing on 5B.7 reliability of information; 5B.10 trajectory assessment methodology).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0035","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"TEPJF partial recount decision and results (237,000 ballots annulled, Calderón margin unchanged at 0.56%). Political conflict over electoral results, not economic governance policy.","exclusion_reason":"Chunk covers electoral tribunal recount process and results. No substantive economic governance policy content for 5B questions."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0036","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"AMLO's escalating defiance: 'se abre el camino a un usurpador,' September 16 CND convention, proclamation as 'presidente legítimo' with alternate cabinet. Political confrontation drama, not governance policy.","exclusion_reason":"Chunk covers political confrontation and 'legitimate president' declaration. No substantive economic governance policy content for 5B questions."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0037","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"AMLO's second marriage to Beatriz Gutiérrez Müller in October 2006, birth of son Jesús Ernesto in April 2007. Pure personal biography, not governance.","exclusion_reason":"Chunk covers personal family event (second marriage) and birth of son. No economic governance content for 5B questions."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0038","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"December 1, 2006 Calderón inauguration with physical confrontation between PAN and PRD legislators.
